body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-M2-CLI-HALF-PINNED-INPUTS"
  title: "M2's CLI half: one precondition refusal reaching a byte-identical envelope from the CLI and from the crate, carried without adding a field to a public DTO"
  epic: "portable-slice"
  component: "Engine"
  module: "wasm-seam"
  status: planned
  priority: high
  tracking_issue: 1355
  dependencies:
    - "#1351 M2 (the measurement this completes)"
    - "the spike report's corrected verdict (M2 is the only outstanding measurement)"

  intent: |
    The spike measured the operation twice and got the same digest twice *in the same runtime*. The
    CLI half was never reached, so the property the whole wasm crate exists to guarantee — the engine
    and its wasm slice decide identically on identical input — is unproven.

    Two facts from the spike make this small rather than large:

    1. **The clock was the only unpinned value in the operation.** One threaded site
       (`pinned_timestamp`) sufficed, not 151. The 94 `Utc::now()` and 57 `Uuid::new_v4()` sites in
       the gate modules are in callers that the operation does not traverse.
    2. **Digest equality is not payload equality.** Unpinned 884 B vs pinned 877 B — a whole-second
       instant serialises shorter than a nanosecond one. A comparison that normalises either side
       hides exactly the difference this measurement exists to find, so nothing may normalise.

    The carrier is the part that needs care. The spike added
    `BuildEnvelopeInput::pinned_timestamp`, which is a **public field on a public, literally
    constructible DTO**, and two other crates in this workspace construct that DTO literally:
    `server/tests/audit_scope_check_verify.rs:20` and `mcp/src/host/mod.rs:681`. Adding a field to a
    non-`#[non_exhaustive]` struct is a breaking change under Rust's semver rules, and it forced 11
    test edits. Making the struct `#[non_exhaustive]` would break those literals harder.

    So the pinned inputs travel in their **own type** through an **additive** method. No existing
    public item gains a field, no existing signature changes, and the four published crates detect
    nothing — which is the same M1b standard the `portable` feature had to meet.

  in_scope:
    - "A new value carrying the pinned instant and the pinned id draws, owned by the engine, additive to the public surface"
    - "An additive factory method that accepts it; `build_and_send` and `BuildEnvelopeInput` keep today's shapes exactly, and `pinned_timestamp` is removed from the DTO"
    - "CLI flags supplying pinned clock and ids, behind a non-default cargo feature, so a default build's behaviour and surface are unchanged"
    - "The envelope factory stamps the pinned instant when one is supplied and reads the wall clock otherwise, so `None` remains today's behaviour"
    - "The M2 measurement, run end to end: one precondition refusal, CLI and in-crate, digests compared with no normalisation"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Threading the seam through the remaining sites (Phase B). The measurement needs the one operation, and the count it recorded is 1"
    - "The wasm side: this issue produces the CLI-side envelope and the comparison; wiring `EngineGate` to it is Phase C"
    - "Conformance goldens, `gate: \"cli\"`, or deleting `normalised_comparison` — untouched here"
    - "A `Clock`/`IdSource` trait pair across the engine. The evidence does not support the abstraction yet: one operation, one site, and the ids in this operation are already supplied through the fixture ports"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "None — no domain type changes; the pinned value is an application input"
    application:
      - "engine/src/audit/application/factory (the additive method) and the envelope factory's timestamp selection"
      - "engine/src/audit/application/dto/mod.rs — `pinned_timestamp` removed from `BuildEnvelopeInput`"
    infrastructure:
      - "cli: the pinned-input flags behind a non-default feature, read into the new value"
    interfaces:
      - "cli: one new flag pair; no existing flag changes"

  citations:
    - file: "engine/src/audit/application/dto/mod.rs"
      note: ":124 `pub pinned_timestamp` — the field this issue removes; the struct is public and not `#[non_exhaustive]`"
    - file: "engine/src/audit/application/envelope_factory_impl.rs"
      note: ":182 `timestamp: input.pinned_timestamp.unwrap_or_else(chrono::Utc::now)` — the single stamping site; it must read the new carrier"
    - file: "server/tests/audit_scope_check_verify.rs"
      note: ":20 a literal `BuildEnvelopeInput { … }` from another crate — the reason a field cannot be added"
    - file: "mcp/src/host/mod.rs"
      note: ":681 the second literal construction, in a published crate"
    - file: "cli/src/cli_boundary/orchestrator.rs"
      note: ":198, :274, :281, :309 `create_default()` — where the pinned inputs reach the factory"

  verification:
    - "`cargo build -p rigorix-engine -p rigorix-mcp -p rigorix-server` succeeds with zero edits to `server/tests/audit_scope_check_verify.rs` and `mcp/src/host/mod.rs`; `git diff --stat` on those two files is empty"
    - "`cargo test -p rigorix-engine -p rigorix-mcp -p rigorix-server` passes unmodified — the same M1b standard"
    - "The CLI, given the pinned fixture, produces an envelope whose sha256 equals the in-crate run's sha256 for the same refusal; both digests and both commands appear in the M2 report"
    - "The comparison normalises nothing: a seeded mismatch of one second in the pinned instant changes the digest (the measurement must fail on it, not absorb it)"
    - "An unpinned CLI run and a pinned CLI run of the same refusal differ in size (884 B vs 877 B today) — recorded as evidence that the pin is load-bearing, not a value that happens to be equal"
    - "Default-feature `cargo run -p rigorix-cli -- run …` behaves exactly as 1.12.1: the flags are behind the feature and absent otherwise"
---

# M2, the CLI half

## Why this is the last measurement standing

| | status |
|---|---|
| M1 dependency surface | holds — 74 crates, no forbidden dependency |
| M1b four published crates | holds once the DTO field is removed (the 11 edits were its plumbing) |
| M2 in-crate | holds — 32211b9d… twice |
| M2 CLI | **not reached** |
| M3 shipped bundle | holds — 1 170 635 B against 1 500 000 B |
| M4 cross-process determinism | holds once the clock is pinned |

One row remains. It is also the row that makes the crate's existence meaningful: without it, "the
browser decides the same as the engine" is a design intention with a digest that only ever compared
the crate to itself.

## The carrier is a semver decision, not a style one

```
$ grep -rn 'BuildEnvelopeInput {' --include=*.rs server/ mcp/
server/tests/audit_scope_check_verify.rs:20:    BuildEnvelopeInput {
mcp/src/host/mod.rs:681:            .build_and_send(BuildEnvelopeInput {
```

Two other crates construct that DTO literally, so a new public field is a breaking change — the
kind that only shows up for a downstream user who never appears in this workspace's test run. A new
type plus an additive method costs nothing by comparison and keeps the four published crates at
1.12.1's surface.

## What the measurement must not do

- **No normalised comparison.** If the two envelopes differ in timestamp width, that is a finding,
  not noise to strip.
- **No re-running until the digests agree.** A flip is a defect; the seed in the criteria exists to
  prove the comparison can fail at all.
- **No widening to the full run.** One refusal, one envelope, two runtimes. The five use cases and
  the demo are downstream of this and stay untouched.
title: M2's CLI half: one precondition refusal reaching a byte-identical envelope from the CLI and from the crate, carried without adding a field to a public DTO

body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-SPIKE-VERDICT-CORRECTED-M2-OUTSTANDING"
  title: "The spike's branch C verdict is falsified: M3 holds on the shipped artifact, and the only outstanding measurement is M2's CLI half"
  epic: "portable-slice"
  component: "Docs"
  module: "wasm-seam"
  status: planned
  priority: high
  tracking_issue: 1354
  dependencies:
    - "the bundle-gate subject fix, which produces the shipped-artifact numbers this report must carry"
    - "#1351 (the report being corrected)"

  intent: |
    `docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md` states a verdict — branch C, "the bundle does not fit" —
    and derives from it a product decision: the demo narrows to verify-only, with gate evaluation
    staying CLI-side. The verdict rests on 1 512 420 B measured against a 1 500 000 B ceiling, and
    that number is the *emitted* artifact, 341 785 B of which consists of a debug `name` section.

    Measured on the artifact a host loads, the bundle is 1 170 635 B — 78.0 % of the ceiling — and
    the module passes all fifteen smoke assertions. The branch table's own condition for firing is
    "the excess is not one trimable dependency". That condition was never established: the trim
    attempted was an LTO profile change, the named trim (`regex`) was never run, and the actual
    excess was a section that ships in no production artifact.

    So branch C did not fire, and the narrowed-demo decision was made on a falsified premise.
    Branch D is not earned either: it requires all four measurements, and M2 reached only its
    in-crate half — the CLI never produced a comparable envelope.

    The report is the artifact of record for this epic. Leaving a withdrawn verdict in it as the
    headline is how a later reader inherits "the engine cannot fit in the browser" as a fact.

  in_scope:
    - "The verdict line and the M1–M4 table carry the shipped-artifact numbers with the commands that produced them: M3 pass at 1 170 635 B / 1 500 000 B; M2 recorded as not reached, naming the CLI half as the reason"
    - "The branch table's C row records that it did not fire, and why — the excess was a debug section, not an untrimable dependency — and the regex trim is recorded as unrun and unnecessary on the shipped artifact"
    - "The next-steps section drops the narrowed-demo decision and names M2's CLI half as the next measurement"
    - "The M1b passage keeps both readings (strict: fails on the seam's 11 test edits; scoped to `portable`: zero edits) and states that the tests needed `pinned_timestamp: None` only because a public DTO gained a field — a carrier that the M2 issue replaces, which removes the edits and the caveat together"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Running M2's CLI half. That is its own issue, and this one only records it as outstanding"
    - "Editing the 84-row inventory. Its contents are unaffected"
    - "Any change to the apparatus branch, which stays linked and unmerged"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "None"
    application:
      - "None"
    infrastructure:
      - "None"
    interfaces:
      - "None"

  citations:
    - file: "docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md"
      note: ":8-10 the verdict paragraph; :180-232 the M3 section; :254 the branch table's C row; :259 the narrowed-demo next step"
    - file: "engine/.pi/portable-inventory.tsv"
      note: "the inventory this report ships with — unchanged"

  verification:
    - "The report's verdict paragraph, rendered, reads that M3 holds on the shipped artifact and names M2's CLI half as the sole outstanding measurement: `sed -n '1,12p' docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md` shows 1 170 635 and no `does not fit`"
    - "`grep -c 'does not fit' docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md` returns 0"
    - "Every number in the M1–M4 table has its command on the same page, and each reproduces when re-run from the merged tree"
    - "The M2 row reads `in part` with the reason, not `holds`: `grep -n 'M2' docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md` shows the CLI half named"
    - "The C row of the branch table contains the measured 1 170 635 and the words for 'did not fire'"
---

# Correct the verdict: M3 holds, M2 is outstanding

## What the report says, and what is measured

| | report | measured on the shipped artifact |
|---|---|---|
| M3 engine-linked bundle | 1 512 420 B → "does not fit" (0.8 % over) | **1 170 635 B**; 78.0 % of the 1 500 000 ceiling |
| the 341 785 B removed | not examined | the `name` custom section — debug symbols |
| the "named trim" | `regex`, unrun | unrun and unnecessary; the excess was not a dependency |
| smoke gate | not run on the trimmed artifact | 15/15 pass, identical to the unstripped run |

`wc -c` on `wasm-bindgen` output counts a file a host never sees. That is the whole of the
correction: not a methodology failure — the report applied the issue's ceiling correctly to the
artifact it had — but a subject mismatch, and the spike's only job was to get the subject right.

## What the correction changes downstream

- **The narrowed demo is withdrawn.** Branch C's decided step ("the browser verifies, the gate stays
  server/CLI-side") was the answer to a size problem that does not exist on the shipped artifact.
  Gate evaluation in the browser remains on the table, contingent on M2.
- **M2 becomes the whole of the remaining question.** Byte identity between the CLI and the crate is
  what makes the browser gate mean anything, and it was reached on one side only. A demo built now
  would demonstrate a link that has never produced a comparable envelope.
- **M1b's caveat resolves by deletion rather than by argument.** The 11 test edits were plumbing for
  a public DTO's new field; removing the field removes the edits, and the strict reading then passes
  without needing the "scoped to `portable`" qualifier.

## What must not happen

The verdict must not be softened into "M3 is close enough". A gate is a comparison against a decided
number, and the number is now met with 22 % headroom on the artifact a host loads. The honest
statement is stronger than the report's: M3 passes, and it passed because the emitted file was
never the deliverable.
title: The spike's branch C verdict is falsified: M3 holds on the shipped artifact, and the only outstanding measurement is M2's CLI half

body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-WASM-BUNDLE-GATES-MEASURE-DEBUG-ARTIFACT"
  title: "The wasm size gates measure an artifact no host ships: 341 785 B of the engine-linked bundle is a debug name section, and 33 485 B of the current budget's subject is the same"
  epic: "portable-slice"
  component: "Wasm"
  module: "wasm-seam"
  status: planned
  priority: high
  tracking_issue: 1353
  dependencies:
    - "#1351 (the spike that produced the measurement this issue corrects)"

  intent: |
    `wasm/ci/check-bundle-size.sh` measures the bytes `wasm-bindgen` emits, and
    `wasm/ci/bundle-budget.txt` records that number as the artifact CI ships. It is not: the
    artifact carries a **custom `name` section** — the wasm debug symbol table — which no
    production host needs and which a trimming step removes. On the empty seam that section is
    33 485 B of 243 366 B (13.8 %); with the engine linked it is **341 785 B of 1 512 420 B
    (22.6 %)**.

    The consequence is not cosmetic. The spike's branch C fired on that number: "the bundle
    does not fit" — a verdict about a debug-profile artifact — and the decided next step was to
    narrow the demo to verify-only. Measured on the artifact a host actually loads, the
    engine-linked bundle is **1 170 635 B, 78.0 % of the 1 500 000 B ceiling**, and it passes all
    fifteen `module-smoke.mjs` assertions identically to the unstripped build.

    A size gate whose subject is not the deliverable is the same defect as #1349 (ten gates
    passing on a 368-byte module with no exports), one layer up: the gate is real, the number is
    real, and the artifact is not the thing anyone ships. The budget file's own note even
    claims a step that never ran — "wasm-bindgen output after wasm-opt" — while `wasm-opt` is
    absent from this machine and from CI.

  in_scope:
    - "A deterministic section-level strip of the `name` custom section, run by the packaging path itself, with no binaryen dependency (`wasm-opt` is absent here and in CI)"
    - "The size gate measures the stripped artifact; `bundle-budget.txt` is re-recorded from it (measured 209 881 B, budget measured + 25 % = 262 351 B) and its note stops claiming a wasm-opt pass"
    - "A presence assertion: the packaged artifact must contain no `name` custom section, mirroring the size assertion so that skipping the strip fails the gate on its own"
    - "The same stripped artifact is what `module-smoke.mjs` and `run-host-verification.sh` load, so the number and the smoke subject are one artifact"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Removing `regex` from the slice. That experiment was the branch table's named trim; it is unnecessary once the ship artifact is measured, and it stays unrun until a size problem exists on the shipped artifact"
    - "Adding `wasm-opt`/binaryen to CI. The strip must be reproducible without it"
    - "Re-recording the budget for the engine-linked build. That number belongs to #1351's M3 re-run, not to this gate's subject"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "None"
    application:
      - "None"
    infrastructure:
      - "The packaging step in wasm/ci/run-wasm-gates.sh (or the strip helper it calls)"
      - "wasm/ci/check-bundle-size.sh — subject changes from emitted bytes to shipped bytes"
      - "wasm/ci/bundle-budget.txt — measured_bytes, budget_bytes, note"
    interfaces:
      - "None — the exported surface is unchanged; the stripped module was verified against all fifteen smoke assertions"

  citations:
    - file: "wasm/ci/bundle-budget.txt"
      note: "measured_bytes: 243366, budget_bytes: 304207, and the note claiming `after wasm-opt`"
    - file: "wasm/ci/check-bundle-size.sh"
      note: ":45-48 reads measured_bytes/budget_bytes from the budget file — the gate enforces whatever number the file holds"
    - file: "wasm/ci/module-smoke.mjs"
      note: "the fifteen assertions the stripped artifact must keep passing"
    - file: "wasm/ci/run-wasm-gates.sh"
      note: "the stage order the strip must join, before the smoke stage loads the module"

  verification:
    - "`bash wasm/ci/run-wasm-gates.sh` exits 0, and the printed measured size is the stripped byte count (209 881 B for the current empty seam, not 243 366 B)"
    - "The packaged artifact contains no custom section named `name`: a `grep -a -c 'name'` is not the check — the gate parses sections and asserts on the section id/name pair, and a fixture binary carrying a name section fails it"
    - "Seed: skip the strip step → the presence assertion fails with exit 1 and names the artifact; the size assertion alone would still pass, which is why the presence assertion exists"
    - "`node wasm/ci/module-smoke.mjs <glue> attempt_run,contract_version,export_artifact_set,open_session` exits 0 against the stripped artifact — verified today: 15/15 pass, identical to the unstripped run"
    - "`bash wasm/ci/run-host-verification.sh` exits 0 against the stripped artifact"
    - "The budget note contains no claim about wasm-opt: `grep -c 'after wasm-opt' wasm/ci/bundle-budget.txt` returns 0"
---

# The size gates measure a debug artifact

## Measured today

All four numbers reproduce bit-exactly; the commands are in the reproduction block.

| artifact | emitted bytes | `name` section | stripped bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty seam (default profile) | **243 366** — matches the committed `measured_bytes` exactly | 33 485 (13.8 %) | **209 881** |
| engine linked (LTO=fat, opt-level=z, panic=abort, codegen-units=1) | **1 512 420** — matches the spike report exactly | 341 785 (22.6 %) | **1 170 635** = 78.0 % of the 1 500 000 ceiling |

Engine-linked section sizes: `code` 763 164 B (50.5 %), `data` 400 735 B (26.5 %), `custom`
341 781 B (22.6 %). The other custom sections are `target_features` (148 B) and `producers`
(112 B); they stay — `target_features` is meaningful to some runtimes and neither is a symbol
table.

The stripped engine-linked module passes the crate's own smoke gate unchanged:

```
✓ module loaded        ✓ attempt_run()        ✓ contract_version()      ✓ export_artifact_set()
✓ open_session()       ✓ no unannounced export ✓ contract_version 1.12.1 ✓ versions agree
✓ artifact_format 1    ✓ no verdict-shaped field ✓ opaque handle        ✓ refusal kind: seal_failed
✓ gate_unavailable     ✓ malformed handle throws
✅ the module exports the contract and answers all four functions     EXIT=0
```

## Reproduction

```sh
# empty seam — reproduces the committed 243 366 exactly
cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p rigorix-gate-wasm
wasm-bindgen --target nodejs --out-dir /tmp/pkg target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/rigorix_gate_wasm.wasm
wc -c < /tmp/pkg/rigorix_gate_wasm_bg.wasm                                  # 243366

# engine linked, trimmed — reproduces the spike report's 1 512 420 exactly
CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=fat CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_OPT_LEVEL=z \
CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_PANIC=abort CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=1 \
  cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p rigorix-gate-wasm --features engine
wasm-bindgen --target nodejs --out-dir /tmp/pkg-z target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/rigorix_gate_wasm.wasm
wc -c < /tmp/pkg-z/rigorix_gate_wasm_bg.wasm                                # 1512420
```

The strip is a section walk — 8-byte header, then `id | LEB128 size | body` — dropping only
`id == 0` whose name is `name`. No tool beyond a shell and one small script.

## Why the presence assertion is the load-bearing one

With `measured_bytes: 209881` and `budget_bytes: 262351`, an *unstripped* 243 366 B artifact still
sits under budget and the size gate passes. Size alone therefore cannot prove the strip ran. The
assertion that can is "this artifact carries no `name` section", and it has to be shown to fire:
skip the strip, run the gates, and the presence check must exit 1 and name the artifact.

## What this issue is not

It does not re-open the regex question, and it does not re-record the engine-linked budget. It
fixes the subject: a size gate is only a gate when the bytes it counts are the bytes a host loads.
title: The wasm size gates measure an artifact no host ships: 341 785 B of the engine-linked bundle is a debug name section, and 33 485 B of the current budget's subject is the same
